questions.stem: A company wants an alert when its monthly AWS spending exceeds, or is forecast to exceed, an amount it sets. Which service should it use?

options.rationale: Cost Explorer analyzes costs but is not where you set spending alerts.
Pricing Calculator estimates costs before you build.
AWS Budgets sends alerts when actual or forecasted costs cross your thresholds.
Billing Conductor customizes billing data for showback and chargeback.

questions.explanation: Budgets can also track usage, Reserved Instance and Savings Plans utilization, and trigger actions.

questions.stem: Which service visualizes and analyzes past AWS costs and usage over time with charts and filters?

options.rationale: Pricing Calculator estimates the cost of planned architectures.
Billing Conductor creates custom billing views for groups of accounts.
Artifact provides compliance reports.
Cost Explorer shows costs and usage over time and can forecast future costs.

questions.explanation: Cost Explorer is for analysis of actual spend; the Pricing Calculator is for estimates.

questions.stem: A company wants to estimate the monthly cost of an architecture before it builds anything on AWS. Which tool should it use?

options.rationale: Pricing Calculator models the cost of AWS services for a planned workload.
Cost Explorer analyzes spending that has already happened.
Budgets tracks spending against thresholds.
The Cost and Usage Report details actual usage and costs.

questions.explanation: Estimate with the Pricing Calculator, track with Budgets, analyze with Cost Explorer.

questions.stem: Which feature of AWS Organizations combines the charges of several accounts into one bill and can provide volume pricing discounts?

options.rationale: SCPs limit permissions in member accounts.
Consolidated billing gives one bill for all accounts and combines usage for volume pricing.
Tags categorize costs but do not combine bills.
IAM Identity Center manages workforce sign-in.

questions.explanation: The management account pays for all member accounts under consolidated billing.

questions.stem: A company wants to see AWS costs broken down by project and by department. What should it do?

options.text: Create a separate IAM user for each project
options.rationale: IAM users do not organize billing data.

options.text: Use a different security group for each department
options.rationale: Security groups control traffic, not cost reporting.

options.text: Tag resources and activate those tags as cost allocation tags
options.rationale: Activated cost allocation tags let you group costs by your own categories.

options.text: Deploy each project in its own AWS Region
options.rationale: Regions are not a substitute for cost categorization.

questions.explanation: Cost allocation tags appear in Cost Explorer and the Cost and Usage Report once activated.

questions.stem: Which provides the most detailed, line-item data about AWS costs and usage, delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket?

options.rationale: Budgets tracks thresholds and alerts.
Pricing Calculator estimates planned costs.
Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations.
The Cost and Usage Report contains the most comprehensive cost and usage data.

questions.explanation: The report can be analyzed with tools such as Amazon Athena or Amazon QuickSight.

questions.stem: A company wants to group its accounts and show each business unit a customized view of its AWS costs, for showback and chargeback. Which service is designed for this?

options.rationale: Billing Conductor customizes billing data and pricing for groups of accounts.
Budgets sets spending thresholds and alerts.
Cost Explorer analyzes costs but does not create custom billing views.
SCPs limit permissions in accounts.

questions.explanation: Billing Conductor supports showback and chargeback workflows.

questions.stem: Which service lets a company centrally manage multiple AWS accounts and apply policies to them?

options.rationale: IAM manages identities within an account.
Organizations groups accounts, applies policies and provides consolidated billing.
AWS Config records resource configurations.
Budgets tracks spending.

questions.explanation: Organizations is the basis for multi-account governance and consolidated billing.

questions.stem: Where can a company see its charges for the current month and download its invoices?

options.rationale: Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements, not invoices.
Trusted Advisor gives recommendations.

options.text: The Bills page of the AWS Billing and Cost Management console
options.rationale: The Billing console shows charges by service and provides invoices.
The Health Dashboard shows service events.

questions.explanation: Billing and Cost Management is the console for bills, payments and cost tools.

questions.stem: Which TWO tools help a company estimate or forecast its AWS costs? (Choose TWO.)

options.rationale: Shield protects against DDoS attacks.
Cost Explorer forecasts future costs from past usage.
Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.
Pricing Calculator estimates planned costs.
Artifact provides compliance reports.

questions.explanation: Estimate before building with the Pricing Calculator; forecast running workloads with Cost Explorer.
